title: Hydrolytic synthesis and structural characterization of five hexanuclear oxo-hydroxo lanthanide clusters

synthesis.procedure: A methanol solution (10 mL) of L (4-amido-3,5-dimethyl-1,2,4-triazole; 0.2301 g, 2.1 mmol) was added to aqueous (5 mL) ErCl3·6H2O (0.7664 g, 2.0 mmol) with stirring. The mixture was refluxed for 5 h and the resulting solution was filtered. Pink crystals of 1 suitable for X-ray diffraction were obtained by evaporation of the filtrate after ca. 80 days. Heating was necessary; the endpoint (pH 6–7) was indicated by incipient formation of a permanent precipitate.
synthesis.time: 5 h reflux; crystals after ca. 80 days
synthesis.vessel_or_method: reflux in methanol/water; filtration; slow evaporation
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: filtered after reflux; pink crystals by evaporation of the filtrate after ca. 80 days

properties.summary: Aqueous UV–Vis of 1 shows seven f–f absorption bands of Er3+. Room-temperature μeff is 9.19 B.M. (calc. 9.58 B.M. for 4I15/2). χM(T) decreases monotonically on cooling (full data in ESI), attributed mainly to ligand-field splitting of Er3+ with possible antiferromagnetic Ln···Ln contributions.

properties.summary: Gd3+ f–f absorptions of 4 are weak and only in the UV, obscured by water. Room-temperature μeff is 7.82 B.M. (calc. 7.94 B.M.). μeff decreases steadily from 300 to 50 K then rapidly below 50 K, indicating dominant antiferromagnetic Gd3+···Gd3+ coupling. Curie–Weiss fit of 1/χM vs T gives C = 7.7 cm3 mol−1 K−1 and θ = −3.8 K.
